title: Aquatic therapy (therapy pool)
what: Therapeutic exercises in a warm pool with an instructor. Water takes the load off your joints and back, so moving is easier.
why: For back and joint pain, after injuries and surgery, after a stroke, and for children with movement problems, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: a session usually lasts 30 to 45 minutes; the course usually runs several weeks
tell_doctor: Skin conditions, wounds, or fungal infections
Heart disease, high blood pressure, or epilepsy
If you cannot swim or are afraid of water

prepare.title: Medical note
prepare.text: Many pools ask for a doctor's note or a skin check. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light meal no later than 1 hour before the session.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Shower with soap before the pool.

bring: A swimsuit and a swim cap
steps: You enter the water by a ladder or a lift
The instructor shows you exercises in the water
You move at your own pace, sometimes with floats and belts
At the end, you relax in the water and get out
feel: The water is warm, and moving is easier than on land
Mild tiredness after the session is normal
after: Dry yourself well, including your hair
Do not go out into the cold right after
red_flags: Dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath in the water: tell the instructor right away

faq.q: Do I need to be able to swim?
faq.a: No. Exercises are done in chest-deep water or with support belts.

faq.q: Can I go during my period?
faq.a: It is usually better to skip those days. Check with the clinic.

reminders.text: Pool session tomorrow. Bring a swimsuit, cap, slippers, and a towel.
